_source: AI-researched venue CANDIDATES for Manchester and Cheshire, awaiting review — never directly edited by the research agent. Populated by a daily scheduled research agent (2026-08, at explicit user request: 'fan out some research agents who's goal is to run every day to find and suggest new businesses... they shouldn't go beyond cheshire and manchester just yet'; bumped from ~3-5/day to 10/day at a later explicit request). See .claude/agents/curia-research-daily.md for the full research brief/rules this agent works under (Hard rule 1 chain/fast-food screening, real coordinates only, no duplicates, Do/Drink/Eat coverage balance). The research agent commits straight to master for this file (no PR — this queue has zero effect on the live app, nothing reads it except the review agent and the admin dashboard's Growth Insights context). A second, independent daily agent (.claude/agents/curia-suggestion-review.md) re-verifies each `pending` entry and is the only thing that ever promotes one into the real docs/data/venues.json, behind its own pull request — see that file's own doc comment for why the human checkpoint lives there instead of here. Each entry mirrors docs/data/venues.json's own raw shape (name/district/type/spend/lat/lon/base/bands/reason) exactly, so a reviewed-and-approved entry can be moved into that file with a straight copy-paste, plus review-only fields (suggestedDate, status, researchNotes) that get stripped on promotion. `district` values must be a real existing district id from docs/data/districts.json (manchester/cheshire metros only) UNLESS the entry is itself proposing a brand-new district — see district-suggestions.json for that case instead; a venue suggestion should never invent a district id that doesn't exist anywhere.
_reviewWorkflow: status starts 'pending' on every new entry. The daily curia-suggestion-review agent changes it to 'approved' (then copies the venue fields into docs/data/venues.json and removes the entry here, as part of its own PR) or 'rejected' (left here with researchNotes explaining why, as a record so the same candidate isn't re-suggested later — curia-research-daily checks every entry here regardless of status before suggesting anything new). A human's actual review happens by reading/merging the review agent's PR, not by editing this file directly, though a human reviewer (or a future admin-dashboard screen) can still hand-edit an entry's status here if needed.

suggestions.name: Clark Art
suggestions.reason: Bill Clark's own gallery on Ashley Road since 1999, deep in L.S. Lowry and the northern painters he's written the books on — a private dealer's eye, not a gallery chain's algorithm.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-03: Clark Art (155 Ashley Road, Hale) closed permanently on 3 October 2024 after 18 years, per Bill Clark's own retirement announcement (reported by Altrincham Today, 'An incredible journey: Clark Art to close after 18 years in Hale village'). The prior research pass's sources (Tripadvisor/Artsy/halebarns.com listings) were stale directory pages that hadn't been updated to reflect the closure. Do not re-suggest — the gallery no longer exists.

suggestions.name: Yang Sing
suggestions.reason: Three floors of a Grade II-listed Princess Street townhouse, family-run since the 1970s — bottomless yum cha that still draws a queue nobody seems to mind.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-03: Yang Sing (34 Princess Street) has been closed since December 2021/early 2022 (kitchen fire, then a lease dispute) and Yang Sing Limited is now in liquidation per Companies House — it never reopened despite the owner's 2022 hope to reopen by 2023/24. The prior research pass's sources (visitmanchester.com, Hardens, Tripadvisor) were stale listings still showing it as an open, operating restaurant. Do not re-suggest unless it demonstrably reopens under new ownership.

suggestions.name: Blue Lobster
suggestions.reason: Italian seafood on the corner of London Road and Brown Street, sourced directly from Rome — a Franciacorta bar downstairs, the kitchen running until midnight upstairs.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-03: Blue Lobster (34 London Road, Alderley Edge) closed permanently in December 2017, less than nine months after its April 2017 opening, following a staff-payment dispute with owner Andrea Zecchino (reported by alderleyedge.com and Manchester Confidential at the time). No evidence of any reopening or trading activity was found in the eight years since. The prior research pass's Tripadvisor/Luxury Lifestyle Magazine sources were leftover listings from the 2017 opening, not current confirmation. Do not re-suggest unless it demonstrably reopens under new ownership.

suggestions.name: Manchester Craft and Design Centre
suggestions.reason: Eighteen working studio boutiques inside a converted Victorian fish and poultry market on Oak Street — watch a maker at the bench, then buy the piece straight from the hands that shaped it.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via manchester.gov.uk's own directory listing, craftanddesign.com (official site, hours Mon-Sat 10am-5.30pm), and Manchester's Finest — 17 Oak Street, M4 5JD, coordinates 53.4844/-2.2356 confirmed against the postcode. A council-supported charity/non-profit arts venue (Companies House: Manchester Craft & Design, a registered charity), single site since its 1980s conversion of the old fish market — not a commercial chain, same category of public single-site cultural venue already seeded here (Manchester Art Gallery, Royal Exchange Theatre). Reuses the existing DESIGN GALLERY type (Rococo, Prestbury) since it fits precisely — no new type needed. Targets Northern Quarter's Do gap (2 of 9 venues before this addition) and brings the district to 10. High confidence.

suggestions.name: The Horsfall
suggestions.reason: A three-storey Victorian shop on Great Ancoats Street, named for the philanthropist who opened the country's first art museum here in 1884 — free exhibitions and open studio sessions, run by the mental health charity that revived the building.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via Creative Tourist, 42nd Street's own site (42ndstreet.org.uk), and Northern Soul — 87-91 Great Ancoats Street, M4 5AG, near the Jersey Street junction, coordinates estimated from the confirmed nearby M4 5AG postcode centroid (53.4827/-2.2287) adjusted toward that junction. Single-site venue run by 42nd Street, a registered mental health charity — not a chain by any measure. Reuses the existing ART GALLERY type (Manchester Art Gallery, esea contemporary, etc.) — fits precisely. Targets Ancoats' Do gap (2 of 8 venues before this addition), bringing the district to 9. High confidence on identity/non-chain status; coordinates are a good-faith street-level estimate rather than a pinpoint address match, consistent with this file's existing precision bar.

suggestions.name: Bar Etna
suggestions.reason: Sicilian, family-run, and unbothered by the market's queues two streets over — fresh pasta and pistachio everything from a kitchen that still mans its own deli counter.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via the venue's own site (baretna.co.uk, 'family-run Sicilian trattoria, deli & coffee shop'), Tripadvisor and Manchester's Finest — 74 Stamford New Road, Altrincham WA14 1BS, coordinates estimated from the confirmed Stamford New Road corridor (matching this file's existing Riddles entry two streets away). No second site found anywhere in searches (unlike Yara or Heddy's, which were explicitly checked and are multi-site) — single-site, family-run, passes Hard rule 1. Reuses the existing ITALIAN RESTAURANT type (Cibo) since Sicilian cooking sits within it. Targets Altrincham's Eat gap (1 of 5 venues before this addition), bringing the district to 6. High confidence.

suggestions.name: Knutcraft at the Ruskin Rooms
suggestions.reason: A Grade II-listed former reading room and fire station on Drury Lane, now a pottery-painting studio running Bring Your Own Bottle evenings for adults who'd rather glaze a plate than scroll past one.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via Historic England's listing entry, knutcraft.co.uk (official site) and Knutsford Town Council's own page on the Ruskin Rooms building — Drury Lane, Knutsford WA16 6HA, coordinates 53.3068/-2.3730 confirmed against the postcode. Single-site independent craft business operating inside a council/heritage-managed listed building — no chain footprint found. Introduces a new type, POTTERY STUDIO (no existing type fits a pottery-painting-and-crafts business precisely) — recommend mapping it to the same 'Cookery & craft' Do tile that COOKERY SCHOOL (Wilmslow Kitchen) already uses, since that tile's own sub-preferences ('Hands-on', 'Expert-led') fit directly. Targets Knutsford's Do gap (1 of 5 venues before this addition), bringing the district to 6. High confidence.

suggestions.name: Mobberley Ice Cream Coffee House
suggestions.reason: A working dairy farm on Church Lane doing its own ice cream, its own coffee roast and a proper afternoon tea — order the sundae, then walk it off past the herd that made it.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via the venue's own site (mobberleyicecream.co.uk, hours Wed-Sun 10am-4pm) and Tripadvisor — Dairy Farm, Church Lane, Mobberley WA16 7RA, coordinates 53.3187/-2.3177 confirmed against the postcode. A single working farm site (The Mobberley Ice Cream Company) — same non-chain profile as Waugh Brow Farm Shop and Barnshaw Smithy, already seeded in this district. Reuses the existing BRUNCH SPOT type (Barnshaw Smithy, Aldeli) since it fits precisely. Targets Mobberley's balanced-but-thin spread (6 venues before this addition, evenly split Do/Drink/Eat), bringing the district to 7. High confidence.

suggestions.name: Yuzu
suggestions.reason: Twenty-five covers on Faulkner Street, no bookings for most sittings, BYOB, and a ramen broth that's been simmering since before Chinatown's newer rooms opened — a queue since 2012 that still hasn't thinned.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via Manchester Confidential's review, Creative Tourist, and Yuzu's own site (yuzumanchester.co.uk) — 39 Faulkner Street, Manchester M1 4EE, coordinates 53.4783/-2.2396 confirmed against the postcode. Established 2010, single site, Michelin Guide-listed 2015-2018 and Good Food Guide 2015-2020 — no second location found anywhere, non-chain. Introduces a new type, JAPANESE RESTAURANT (no existing tile/type fits an izakaya-style Japanese restaurant precisely) — left Eat category-only, same precedent as CANTONESE ROAST/DIM SUM/INDIAN RESTAURANT elsewhere in this district's own real venues. Chinatown's real gap is Do/Drink (1 each of 5 venues before this addition) rather than Eat (3 of 5) — a good-faith search for a Chinatown Do or Drink candidate this run turned up nothing that cleared Hard rule 1 (the one live-lead, Seven Oaks, is a sports-bar/late hospitality-industry venue that doesn't match this app's register; XiongQi Hot Pot is a 7-site UK chain, rejected) or was independently confirmable as still operating (Chinese Arts Centre/CFCCA has since rebranded and relocated to esea contemporary, already seeded in Northern Quarter; a 'Chinatown Heritage Centre' referenced in secondary listicles could not be independently verified as a real, current Manchester venue — likely confusion with Singapore's attraction of the same name). Yuzu is included anyway as a genuinely exceptional, thoroughly verified Eat venue rather than leaving Chinatown's count unpadded for its own sake; Do/Drink remain open gaps for a future run. High confidence on Yuzu itself.

suggestions.name: One Eight Six
suggestions.reason: A barbershop by day on the old Deansgate courthouse corner; find the mirrored door after dark and it's live soul and Motown running until the small hours.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via Manchester's Finest, oneeightsix.co.uk (official site) and Flickr/architectural sources confirming the building — 186 Deansgate, M3 3WB, at the corner with Hardman Street (the Grade II-listed former County Courts building). Coordinates estimated toward that corner given no exact geocode was returned; the postcode's own ward is confirmed Deansgate. Single site, independent concept (barbershop-by-day/live-music-bar-by-night) under local operator Dean Mac — no chain footprint found. Reuses the existing COCKTAIL BAR type. Targets Deansgate's balanced-but-thin spread (6 venues before this addition, 2 Do/2 Drink/2 Eat). Medium-high confidence: identity and non-chain status are solid, coordinates are a street-corner estimate rather than a geocoded pinpoint.

suggestions.name: Arcane
suggestions.reason: A basement two friends built off King Street, no sign worth mentioning above ground — cocktails poured without the queue Deansgate's louder rooms carry.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via Tripadvisor, Yelp and Manchester Union Brewery's own site (which stocks it) — 2 South King Street, M2 6DQ, confirmed as sitting within the Deansgate electoral ward; coordinates 53.4805/-2.2465 reflect the confirmed general King Street-area position. Independent, opened and run by named owners Mark Taylor and Gary Kilroy — single basement site, no chain footprint found. Reuses the existing COCKTAIL BAR type. Second Deansgate addition this run alongside One Eight Six, both Drink — Deansgate's own Do/Eat gaps remain for a future pass, but both cleared verification cleanly where several other Deansgate leads this run did not (Motley is YOTEL-hotel-branded, dropped as chain-adjacent; WOOD & Company confirmed permanently closed October 2024). Medium-high confidence.

suggestions.name: KLUB
suggestions.reason: A one-woman-built rooftop salon above Manchester Hall's old Freemasons' hall — one-to-one treatments, not a treatment-room timetable to fit yourself around.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via Treatwell, Fresha (booking platforms listing the venue directly) and the salon's own site (klub-salon.co.uk) — 5th Floor, Manchester Hall, 36 Bridge Street, M3 3BT, coordinates 53.4809/-2.2501 confirmed against the postcode. Independently owned and run (named owner-operator), single site — not a chain. Introduces a new type, BEAUTY SALON (no existing type fits a boutique hair/beauty salon rather than a full day spa) — recommend mapping it to the same 'Spa & wellness' Do tile that SPA already uses, since that tile's 'Treatments' sub-preference fits directly. Targets Spinningfields' Do gap (2 of 7 venues before this addition), bringing the district to 8. High confidence on identity/non-chain status; a strong candidate found earlier in this district's research, Artzu Gallery, was dropped on discovering it has since relocated out of Spinningfields to Castlefield.

suggestions.name: Portland Wine
suggestions.reason: An Ashley Road institution that still runs its own tastings — a glass of fizz on arrival, five wines poured properly, and a port to finish before you've decided what to take home.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via Companies House (Portland Wine Company Limited, incorporated 2011, single registered office) and the venue's own events page and Facebook — 152a Ashley Road, Hale, WA15 9SA, coordinates estimated from the confirmed Ashley Road corridor (matching this file's existing Hale Wine Bar/Contemporary Six Hale entries on the same road). No evidence of a second shop location found in any source checked, though no source explicitly states 'single site' either — treated as medium confidence on the chain-footprint question specifically (identity and current trading are high confidence: it runs its own ticketed tastings, e.g. a recent Spanish wine evening and a Winter Wine Fair). Introduces a new type, WINE MERCHANT (a wine shop that runs in-house tastings sits between the 'Wine bars' tile and a straightforward off-license) — left Drink category-only for now, same precedent as ALE HOUSE. Targets Hale's thin spread (7 venues before this addition), bringing the district to 8.
